strings: Get the Social Security number and card
You requested it on the hospital form. Nothing else is needed unless the card has not arrived, and it blocks the tax return, the $1,000 newborn account and most bank accounts until it does.
No legal deadline. Ask SSA what to expect for this request and record that date in the follow-up section rather than relying on a bundled turnaround time.
Social Security: numbers for children
https://www.ssa.gov/number-card/
Order certified copies of the birth certificate

Issued by Puerto Rico, not by the hospital and not federally. Ask the issuing office how many certified copies your family needs and whether ordering them together is useful. Office: Puerto Rico vital records office. We do not carry a specific office for this place yet, so the link goes to the national directory rather than to one we would be guessing at.
No legal deadline. Ask the issuing office when the record and certified copies will be ready, because filing and processing times differ by jurisdiction.
USAGov: order a birth certificate
https://www.usa.gov/birth-certificate
Add the baby to the Acme PPO plan

This is the hardest date in the whole list, and it is handled by your employer's benefits administrator rather than by any website. Federal rules give you at least 30 days from the birth, and the plan then has to make coverage effective from the date of birth, which is what makes the hospital bill get paid. Outside the window you are waiting for open enrollment. You said to contact: benefits@acme.example.

Federal rules give at least 30 days after a birth to request enrollment in a job-based plan, and coverage is then effective from the birth date. Your plan may allow longer. Ask your benefits administrator for the exact date and work to whichever is sooner.
Department of Labor: special enrollment after a birth
https://webapps.dol.gov/elaws/ebsa/health/72.asp
Report the birth to the Marketplace and add the baby

Reporting the birth is also what re-runs your savings: a larger household usually changes the premium tax credit, and the change does not happen on its own. Marketplace coverage for a new baby is generally backdated to the date of birth, and it is not in force until the first premium is paid. You have not said which marketplace you use. About a third of states run their own site rather than HealthCare.gov, and signing in to the wrong one costs days inside a window that does not stop for it, so start from the state picker below.

Marketplace special enrollment after a birth is 60 days. If your state runs its own marketplace, that window is the same but the site, the account and the documents are your state's, so do this there rather than on HealthCare.gov and confirm the date while you are in it.
Find your state's Marketplace
https://www.healthcare.gov/marketplace-in-your-state/
Apply for Medicaid or CHIP coverage

Medicaid and CHIP take applications at any time of year, so there is no window to miss here. Eligibility and the agency are set by Wyoming, and children qualify at higher household incomes than adults do.
No enrollment window. Applications are accepted year-round.
HealthCare.gov: Medicaid and CHIP
https://www.healthcare.gov/medicaid-chip/getting-medicaid-chip/
Find out which enrollment window applies to you

This is the only unanswered question in your plan that costs money. A job-based plan has to give at least 30 days from the birth and the Marketplace gives 60, and both start the coverage on the day of the birth, which is what gets the hospital bill paid. Medicaid and CHIP take applications all year, so if that is the answer there is nothing to miss. Find out which one it is, then set it in your household answers and the real deadline appears here.

Not a deadline anyone set: the shortest real window is 30 days, so answering this inside a fortnight leaves room to actually use it. Baby Docs will not put a red date or a reminder on a window it cannot name.
Change the dependent care FSA election

A birth may let your employer plan permit a dependent care FSA election change, and it is separate from the medical plan. Ask the benefits administrator for the plan's qualifying-event rule and window before assuming an election is available or locked until open enrollment.

Your plan sets this window, not the IRS, and 30 days is only the commonest version of it. Ask your benefits administrator or read the plan document for your own date, and work to that. This app will not put a red date on a number it cannot check.
IRS: child and dependent care expenses
https://www.irs.gov/publications/p503
Confirm whether parentage paperwork applies

You chose not to answer the parentage question. This task does not assume that paperwork applies. Ask the hospital birth registrar or your state's vital records or child-support agency whether anything is needed for this birth record, especially if a parent is not on the record or the situation is contested. This app will not prepare or file a legal form for you.
No date is invented here. The office handling the birth record can tell you whether a form applies and what its own timing is.
Find your state's child support agency
https://acf.gov/css/contact-information/state-and-tribal-child-support-agency-contacts
Establish the second parent on the record

This is legally significant and it is state law, so Puerto Rico sets the form, the witnessing and the window in which a signature can be withdrawn. It affects the birth record, inheritance, benefits and custody.

The fastest door is the hospital's birth registrar before discharge; after that it is usually the state vital records office or the child support agency, and the directory below is how to find the one for Puerto Rico. Ask how long a signature can be withdrawn before you sign, not after.

This app will not prepare or file it for you, and if anything about the situation is contested or either parent is unsure, that is a conversation with a lawyer rather than a form to sign today.
Usually signed at the hospital. It can be done later, but rescission windows and the process for adding a parent afterwards are state-specific and get harder with time.
Check the name and details on the certificate

Read the certified copy against what you intended: spelling of Rosa's name, the date, and the parent details. Ask the issuing office how corrections, amendments, fees and time limits work where the record was issued. Every document downstream is built from this one.
Correction windows and fees are set by the state that issued the record. Checking early is what keeps a fix inside the free window.
Puerto Rico vital records office
Get the newborn screening results in writing

Every state screens newborns for a panel of conditions, plus hearing and a heart-oxygen check. Ask the pediatric practice or state programme where the results are held and how to obtain a copy for your own file. If anything is out of range, the practice or the state health department contacts you: this task is not how you would find out, and Baby Docs does not read, hold or interpret a result.
No deadline. Ask the pediatric practice when the results will be available and record that date in the follow-up section if you need to chase them.
Newborn screening in your state
https://newbornscreening.hrsa.gov/your-state
File the parental leave claim

FMLA protects the job but is unpaid, and eligibility depends on the employee and employer. Whether anything is paid depends on the employer's policy and the paid-leave programme in the state where the parent works. Ask the employer which work-state programme, notice rule and form apply; this household residence answer is not enough to determine it.
FMLA itself has no filing deadline for the employee. Ask the employer for the notice window and the work-state programme's own date before relying on one.
Department of Labor: FMLA
https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla
File the second parent's leave claim

A separate claim, with a separate employer and possibly a separate work-state programme. Bonding leave for the non-birth parent can be governed by different rules than the birth parent's own leave, so the two dates cannot be assumed to match. Assign this one to whoever is filing it and ask that employer which jurisdiction and notice rule apply.
FMLA sets no filing deadline for the employee. Ask the second parent's employer for its notice window and the applicable work-state programme's own date.
Update tax withholding at work
A dependent changes what should be withheld. Nothing is lost by leaving it, but the money sits with the IRS until you file instead of arriving in the paychecks you need it in.
No deadline. The sooner it changes, the more paychecks it affects.
IRS: Form W-4
https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-4
Check the hospital billed under the baby's own coverage

Ask the insurer how newborn claims should be billed under this plan, then compare the explanation of benefits with the hospital bill. Do not assume that a bill showing Rosa as uninsured tells you who owes it or why. Call the insurer before paying, and follow the denial notice's instructions if a claim is refused.
No deadline of its own, but appeal windows run from the date on the denial notice or explanation of benefits, so it is worth catching early.
HealthCare.gov: appeal an insurance decision
https://www.healthcare.gov/appeal-insurance-company-decision/appeals/
Claim the $1,000 newborn account

US citizen children born from 2025 through 2028 may qualify for a one-time $1,000 federal contribution. The election needs a Social Security number issued to the child first, so this one is waiting on the SSN card. Two other conditions sit behind it and only the instructions can settle them: no election having been made for this child already, and the person electing expecting to claim them for the tax year. The IRS calls these Trump Accounts, which is the name on the form and on irs.gov.

The current Form 4547 instructions set no filing deadline: the election can be made at any time, including with a return. They also say no pilot contribution is deposited before 4 July 2026. Read the current instructions before relying on any date, because a wrong date on a one-time $1,000 election is worse than no date.
IRS: the official page
https://www.irs.gov/trumpaccounts
Claim the baby on your next tax return

A baby born at any point in 2028 counts as a dependent for the whole of 2028. The Child Tax Credit needs a valid SSN for the child issued before the return's due date, which is the real reason the SSN task sits at the top of this list. Whether you qualify depends on facts this app does not hold, so check the year you are filing for or ask whoever prepares the return.
Handled when you file. Listed here so the SSN and childcare paperwork are gathered before the return, not during it.
IRS: Child Tax Credit
https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/child-tax-credit
Open a 529 college savings account

Optional and entirely yours to time. Worth checking whether Wyoming gives a state income tax deduction for its own plan before picking one, because that is usually the only reason to prefer a home-state plan. Baby Docs does not recommend a plan or a provider.
No deadline. Open it whenever you want to.
IRS: qualified tuition programs
https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc313
Apply for the baby's first passport
Blocked until the certified birth certificate arrives, because the application submits the original. Every child under 16 applies in person, with a parent present to sign.
No deadline. Driven by when you plan to travel.
USAGov: passport for a child
https://www.usa.gov/child-passport
Update beneficiaries on life insurance and retirement accounts

Beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and life insurance override a will, so this is not covered by writing one. Naming a minor directly has consequences worth understanding first, which is usually why people name a trust or a custodian instead. Baby Docs is not a financial adviser and this is a prompt, not advice.
No deadline. Listed at 90 days because it is the task everyone agrees to do and nobody does.
Name a guardian in a will

The nomination of a guardian for a minor is made in a will, and without one a court chooses. Requirements for a valid will are state law. This app tracks the task and nothing else: it does not draft or store legal documents, and the questions this raises are for a lawyer.
No deadline. Ninety days is a prompt, not a rule.
Set up the pediatric patient portal

The portal is where the immunization record lives, and daycare, school and travel all ask for it eventually. Federal law gives you the right to a copy of your child's record whether or not the practice runs a portal. Both parents should have their own login rather than sharing one.
No deadline.
How to get a health record
https://www.healthit.gov/how-to-get-your-health-record
Get on childcare waitlists

Not paperwork the government asks for, and on this list only because the waits are measured in months and the deposits are usually refundable. Your state's child care resource and referral agency also holds the list of financial help, which is worth a look before you pay a deposit. Nothing here is time-critical in the way the insurance window is.
Childcare.gov: find child care
https://childcare.gov/
